headline: Attachment printing and Spectrum mail failures drive an August support surge that Thunderbird engineering must triage first
narrative_md:
Support volume rose from 731 questions in July to 940 in August, a jump of 209. No brand new problem clusters appeared. The growth came from existing clusters getting much worse after the 153 and 154 releases. Attachments questions more than tripled, from 17 to 55. Performance and crash questions more than doubled, from 29 to 69.

The sharpest new pain is rank 1, blank pages when printing PDF and email attachments. It went from 1 question to 38 in one month. Only 37 percent of those threads reached a resolution, meaning support had no working fix to give. This pattern points at a print or PDF rendering regression, that is a bug introduced by the 154 release. Rank 7, broken drag and drop of messages and attachments to the file system after 153, points at the same release window and likely shares a file handling root cause.

The most severe pain sits with one provider. Rank 2 covers Spectrum, Charter and Roadrunner mail download and connection failures. Thirty one of its 34 questions scored severity 4 or higher, so users lost mail access entirely. This looks like a server side authentication or TLS change at the provider, not a Thunderbird build issue, but Thunderbird must confirm and publish guidance.

Two credential clusters are served worst. Rank 11, Yahoo, AT&T and AOL password rejections, resolved only 29 percent of the time. Rank 9, repeated password prompts, left 42 percent of users with no reply at all. Both suggest gaps in app specific password handling and in stored credential renewal.

issues.why: Printing attachments as blank pages jumped from 1 to 38 questions and only 37 percent of users got a fix.
issues.action: Engineering must bisect print and PDF viewer changes in the 154 release and reproduce blank output across Windows print drivers.

issues.why: Spectrum, Charter and Roadrunner users lost mail access outright, with 31 of 34 reports at the top severity band.
issues.action: Engineering must capture connection logs from affected accounts and check for a provider side authentication, port or TLS change.

issues.why: The missing Send button and compose toolbar hit 28 users, up from 8, though 89 percent got a workaround.
Startup hangs tied to the System Integration dialog reached 22 reports at 4.2 mean severity, and 23 percent of askers got no reply.
issues.action: Engineering must review the default mail client check on startup for a blocking call and add a timeout.

issues.why: Freezes and crashes during normal use grew to 25 reports with 20 at high severity.
issues.action: Engineering must pull crash and hang signatures from 153 and 154 telemetry and compare against message load paths.

issues.why: Total send and receive failure carries the highest mean severity at 4.5 and leaves 29 percent of askers unanswered.
issues.action: Engineering must check whether these reports overlap with rank 2 or form a separate connection stack regression.

issues.why: Drag and drop of messages and attachments to the file system broke after 153, moving from 1 report to 16.
issues.action: Engineering must test file drag targets on all three desktop platforms against the 153 file handling changes.

issues.why: Stored password recovery requests rose to 26 and 31 percent of those users received no answer.
issues.action: Engineering must review whether the password manager exposes saved credentials clearly enough after recent profile changes.

issues.why: Repeated password prompts despite saved credentials resolved only 42 percent of the time and left 42 percent unanswered, the worst reply rate on the list.
issues.action: Engineering must trace token refresh and credential store reads when a saved password exists but the server rejects it.

issues.why: Blank message bodies reached 19 reports with 13 at high severity and only 47 percent resolved.
issues.action: Engineering must check message rendering and remote content handling for a regression that empties the reading pane.

issues.why: Yahoo, AT&T and AOL password rejections resolved just 29 percent of the time, the worst outcome of any cluster.
issues.action: Engineering must add an in product prompt that detects these providers and guides users to create an app specific password.

issues.why: Disappearing folders and messages fell from 35 to 28 reports but still leaves half of users unresolved and 29 percent unanswered.
issues.action: Engineering must review local folder index rebuilds and IMAP subscription state for silent folder loss.
